visual.general_description: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram tracing on pink grid paper with a lead II rhythm strip.
visual.detailed_description: A standard twelve-lead electrocardiogram on pink grid paper in a three-row by four-column layout with a long bottom rhythm strip. Column one is I, II, III; column two aVR, aVL, aVF; column three V1, V2, V3; column four V4, V5, V6; the bottom strip is labelled II. A rectangular calibration pulse starts each row. The rhythm looks regular with narrow QRS complexes. In V1 and V2 the QRS is mainly negative after a small initial positive deflection, with the J point lifted above the baseline and the ST segment sloping downward toward a shallow T wave; V3 shows an upright T wave and V4 to V6 have tall upright QRS complexes with upright T waves. No text other than lead labels is visible.

visual.general_description: Three stacked panels (A, B, C) of dark-background electrophysiology-system recordings with white multichannel traces: A transition from beats to rapid arrhythmia, B sustained rapid activity, C large disturbance then regular beats.
visual.detailed_description: Top band of a dark-background electrophysiology recording screen with many stacked white traces, the letter A at the upper left and partly legible lead labels at the left edge. Overlaid on-screen text near the top is partly legible and includes "Arrhythmia Induction" and "Print Review 12 Lead"; small printed numbers (some partly legible, not transcribed) and a light-blue horizontal marker line cross the tracing. At the left a few separated narrow beats appear, followed by wide complexes with changing morphology at a faster rate, then continuous rapid undulating oscillations on all traces toward the right. Middle band with the letter B at the upper left: stacked white traces on a dark background showing continuous, rapid, fairly regular undulating waves across the whole width, larger in the lower precordial group of traces. Partly legible overlaid text reading "Print Review 12 Lead" appears near the top left; small printed numbers along a light-blue marker line are small and partly legible, not transcribed. Bottom band with the letter C at the upper left: the left portion shows large chaotic high-amplitude deflections and vertical white spikes across all traces, followed by a stretch where most traces go flat, then regularly spaced narrow beats on the lower traces. Small printed numbers above some beats (some partly legible, not transcribed) and a light-blue marker line are present.
